text:
jamie: quick thread: thinking out loud about an alternative to the global async handoff queue. small-batch chat p99 is getting hammered by noisy async writes. idea: prefetch-priority lanes + tenant-isolated small-worker pools. feedback?

noel: love the idea. can you sketch how lanes work? is it purely worker isolation or also admission + priority tagging on requests?

jamie: two parts: 1) admission: classify requests into low-latency vs throughput buckets (heuristic: tokens<=8 OR client-specified low_latency=true). 2) execution lanes: each lane has its own bounded async queue + tiny worker set. low-latency lane gets higher scheduling priority on CPU and network IO. fallback: when low-latency lane is full, do a quick best-effort prefetch + return a "soft residency" token.

anya: how do we define "soft residency" without breaking caller assumptions? product will be picky about guarantees.

jamie: 'soft residency' would be explicit in the residency token metadata: { residency: "soft", valid_until: ts } and runtime promises a background prioritized refetch within X ms. client can choose to accept soft or explicitly request strict residency.

pradeep: that sounds similar to stale reads. concern: correctness for tools that rely on strict residency (retrieval, reranking). we could gate soft tokens only for known low-latency SDK flags.

stef: operationally I worry about memory churn. tiny worker pools mean more host staging churn if we mis-size pools. need an autoscaler that looks at small-batch qps and hotset reuse.

jamie: agreed. propose a hybrid: lane worker pools start minimal (2 workers), track warm-hit rate (how often prefetch avoids sync write), scale up to configured max (8) by PID in steps. use exponential backoff for scale-down.

noel: metric set we need: per-lane queue depth, per-lane sync-write count, per-tenant soft-residency-issued, p99 latency per-lane. also add a histogram of prefetch latency vs request latency.

anya: also record "stale-refetch-latency" (time between soft token issuance and background completion). important to set slos.

jamie: example config prototype: ```
PREFETCH_LANES = [
  {"name": "lowlat", "max_workers": 8, "max_queue": 512, "priority": 100},
  {"name": "bulk", "max_workers": 32, "max_queue": 8192, "priority": 10},
]
PREFETCH_RULES = ["tokens<=8 => lowlat", "tokens>8 => bulk"]
```

pradeep: fallback behavior if lowlat lane saturates? you mentioned best-effort prefetch + soft token. What if that fails? sync write is still fallback?

jamie: prefer not to sync-write in the hotpath. fallback plan: a) try cross-tenant steal from underutilized lowlat pools (short-lived) b) if steal fails, return a soft token with immediate background high-priority refetch and a response trace tag. only if the request declares strict_residency=true we block and do sync-write.

stef: cross-tenant steal could be risky for noisy neighbor fairness. we'd need tenant quotas and preemptible tokens. maybe better to have a shared emergency pool with strict accounting.

noel: +1 to emergency pool. keep it global but metered by tenant tokens, consumed only when lanes are saturated. implement as a token bucket per-tenant so we avoid being blown out by one tenant.

anya: how do we handle fragmentation? small-worker pools may increase fragmentation because of many short-lived staging pages. can we add a compaction/aging schedule that runs lower-priority compaction specifically for lowlat lane allocations?

jamie: yes. propose tagging allocations with lane origin and kid of allocation (ephemeral vs long-lived). compaction scheduler will prefer to compact ephemeral allocations during low util epochs. we can use a 'cooldown' window to avoid compacting pages that will be immediately reused.

pradeep: also think about offload: if lowlat lane pages are host-backed and we do background writes, ensure they are pinned briefly until background confirms. otherwise risk refetch storms.

jamie: plan: background refetch job will pin the page in host staging for at least min_pin_ms (e.g., 200ms) and then release; that reduces immediate refetch loops.

noel: curious about telemetry tagging: we need to be able to answer "was p99 caused by lane saturation or by sync write fallback". include fields in traces: lane_used, fallback_type (none|soft|sync), prefetch_elapsed_ms.

stef: let's be careful with trace volume. track tags at sampling rate 1% and full metrics counters separately.

anya: rollout strategy: behind runtime feature flag per-cluster. start with lab tenants on staging, then low-volume prod tenants, monitor sync-write count and p99 delta.

jamie: agreed. I'll prototype: code + config + basic metrics. question: do we want lane decisions purely heuristic or allow client SDK to opt-in?

pradeep: both. heuristic default to cover existing apps, SDK opt-in for advanced customers. requires API surface to specify latency_class: low|normal|bulk.

noel: docs: we need to document semantics of soft residency and the cost model (background refetch cost) so product and sales can communicate.

jamie: I'll draft RFC with: goals, admission rules, lane configs, fallback semantics, metrics, rollout plan, and a perf experiment plan.

ops-bot: deploy queued: jamie/prefetch-lanes-proto -> staging in ~7m :rocket:

stef: thanks. one action item: jamie, add a simple unit-test that simulates lane saturation and verifies soft-token issuance vs sync-write when strict flag toggled.

jamie: noted. will post RFC link and staging telemetry after the run finishes.
